name: Vision encoder runs on separate schedule from decoder
symptom: The vision encoder and LLM decoder run on separate schedules, leading to underutilization. While the encoder is running, the decoder is idle, and vice versa.
root_cause: The vision encoder is a separate forward pass that must complete before the LLM prefill can start. Engines that do not overlap these phases leave the GPU underutilized.
workaround: Use an engine with explicit encoder-decoder overlap. TRT-LLM has a Multimodal Encoder Side Stream that prefetches encoder work on a separate CUDA stream. This overlaps the vision encoder forward pass with the LLM's text prefill, improving utilization.
notes: ENCODER-DECODER OVERLAP IS CRITICAL FOR UTILIZATION: Without it, the vision encoder and LLM prefill run serially, leaving the GPU idle during each phase. TRT-LLM's Multimodal Encoder Side Stream prefetches encoder work on a separate CUDA stream, overlapping it with the LLM's text prefill. This is especially important for high-resolution images where the encoder cost is significant. The overlap can improve throughput by 20-30% for vision-language workloads. The mechanism is from TRT-LLM docs; the utilization analysis is derived from the vision encoder FLOP counts.
